title: Finite coefficient tensor maps are surjective modulo the model maximal ideal
statement: Let $A_0,A,C,B$ be commutative local rings. Let $\alpha:A_0\to A$, $\gamma:A_0\to C$, $\varphi:A\to B$, $\psi:C\to B$ be local maps with $\psi\gamma=\varphi\alpha$. Use $\alpha,\gamma$ as the algebra structures and assume $A$ is finite over $A_0$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $D=C\otimes_{A_0}A$ [def-weil-module-base-change] and let $F:D\to B$ be a ring map with $F(c\otimes a)=\psi(c)\varphi(a)$. If $C\to B/\mathfrak m_A B$ induced by $\psi$ is surjective, then $D\to B/\mathfrak m_C B$ induced by $F$ is surjective. Neither completeness, Noetherianity, formal smoothness, nor flatness is required.

source.place: Remark 07NS parts (1),(3), nilpotent Nakayama argument; steps 4 and the finite iteration in step 6 of lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-over-finite-coefficient-map.

proof.text: The images of a finite A₀-module generating set generate A/m₀A over k₀. Thus A/m₀A is finite-dimensional over k₀ and Artinian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian]. It is local, since m₀A lies in m_A. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] its maximal ideal is nilpotent: m_A^N ⊆ m₀A for some positive N.

Put T=F(D), a subring containing ψ(C) and φ(A) by the pure-tensor formula. The hypothesis says B=ψ(C)+m_A B. Expand any element of m_A^i B as a finite sum φ(x_j)b_j with x_j ∈ m_A^i, and decompose each b_j by this equality. The ψ(C) terms belong to T and the remainders to m_A^(i+1)B. Starting at i=0 and iterating gives B=T+m_A^N B.
The previous power containment gives m_A^N B ⊆ m₀B. Compatibility and locality of γ give m₀B ⊆ m_C B. Hence B=T+m_C B, which means every quotient class has an F-preimage.
